description:
It's big game night at the ballpark, and everybody shows off their outfit before revealing what they really do at work: the hot dog vendor, the bat dog and the kiss camera.
Everyone except Gordon, the grumpy groundskeeper. He has a secret under that rain jacket.

lines.text: Outfit check. Big game night. Then you see where I work.
Nobody needs to see you sell a hot dog, Tee.
Gordon. The internet needs this. Look at the sparkle.
You look like a disco ball that got a job.
Thank you. Camera, roll it.
I am a kiss camera. I do not roll. I glide.
Sparkle jacket. Gold boots. And where do I work?
Section four hundred and twelve. Hot dogs! Get your hot dogs!
She threw a hot dog forty rows.
I have an arm. They should sign me.
It hit the guy in the bird hat.
He caught it with his face. He's happy. Look at him.
He is eating it off his own hat. Very resourceful.
Slugger. Your turn. Outfit first.
Tie. Cap. A little cologne. Grass flavored.
He rolled in my infield.
I was getting into character, Gordon.
And the work reveal?
I am the bat dog. I carry the bat back. On television.
Nine million people watch him jog.
I jog with purpose. I wink at the dugout. They feel seen.
Kiss Cam. Outfit check.
Lens cap. Freshly cleaned. I feel expensive.
And the work?
I find two people sitting together and I ruin their evening.
Last night it found me and my rake.
The crowd demanded it, Gordon. Forty thousand people chanting.
I am married. The rake is a coworker.
Then it found you and the dog.
We shared a moment. He gave me a biscuit.
I gave the crowd a hug. Then I went home and stared at a wall.
Okay, everybody did it except one grumpy man.
I don't do outfit checks. I do dirt.
Come on. Big game night. One reveal.
Do it, Gordon. I smelled your locker. I know things.
Fine. One outfit check.
Rain jacket. Old cap. And under the jacket...
Is that a tuxedo?
I wear it every game night. Nobody ever asks.
And the work reveal? We know. You rake the dirt.
I rake the dirt until the third inning.
Then I go in the tunnel. And I put on the head.
What head?
The bird. The big blue bird who dances on the dugout.
You are Captain Feathers?
Do not say his name at work.
I told you. I smelled the feathers.
Twenty two years. He does the splits on the dugout.
You've been dancing for forty thousand people every night and you won't do one outfit check?
The bird is a professional. Gordon is a private person.
I'm about to cry in a sparkle jacket.
Seventh inning. The bird is late. The crowd is looking around.
Tee. My knees are done. Tonight the feathers are yours.
Me? I sell hot dogs!
You threw one forty rows. You're ready.
Outfit check, Tee. You're a bird now.
Big game night. Work reveal. I'm the bird.
And here comes the kiss camera. Gordon and his rake.
Fine. One time.
